column3: Close to the Hebrew; “he became guilty by Baal” is rendered “he offended through Baal worship.”
Close to the Hebrew; “sacrificers of humankind” (or “those among men who sacrifice”) is rendered “the men who sacrifice,” and “molten image” is made plural.
Close to the Hebrew; “from a window” is rendered “from a chimney.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a deliverer” is rendered “Savior.”
Close to the Hebrew; “according to their pasture” is rendered “When they had pasture.”
Close to the Hebrew; “I became” is rendered “I will be.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the cavity of their heart” is rendered “their rib cage.”
NKJV renders the difficult “it destroys you, O Israel, for [you are] against me, against your helper” as “O Israel, you are destroyed, But your help is from Me”; the meaning is uncertain.
NKJV reads the opening word as “I will be” (“I will be your King; Where is any other”), where it is usually read “where is your king?”
Close to the Hebrew; “I gave … so I may take away” is rendered as past, “I gave … took him away.”
Close to the Hebrew; “at the time he does not present himself at the breaking forth of children” is rendered “he should not stay long where children are born”; the meaning is uncertain.

NKJV renders the questions “Shall I ransom them … ? Where are your plagues, O death?” as statements, “I will ransom them … O Death, I will be your plagues!”, reading “where” as “I will be”; “Sheol” is rendered “the grave.”
Close to the Hebrew; “though he flourishes [among] brothers” is rendered “Though he is fruitful among his brethren.”
MT 14:1. Close to the Hebrew; “its pregnant women” is rendered “their women with child.”
